html:
Volga Bulgaria was a state of the Bulgars where the Kama river meets the Volga, in what is now central Russia, from about the 800s to 1236. Its capital was Bolghar.

The Bulgars were a Turkic people of the steppe. When their older realm near the Black Sea broke up in the 600s, one group went west and founded Bulgaria on the Danube while another moved north up the Volga, at first under the Khazars.

Volga Bulgaria controlled the trade of the middle Volga: furs, honey, slaves and wax from the northern forests went south, and silver came north from the Islamic world. In 922 its ruler accepted Islam, an event recorded by the envoy Ibn Fadlan sent from Baghdad. It traded and fought with Kievan Rus'.

The Mongols crushed it in 1236, and it became part of the Golden Horde. Its towns lived on, and the later Khanate of Kazan grew in its land. Volga Tatars and Chuvash count the Bulgars among their ancestors.
sum: Volga Bulgaria was a state of the Bulgars where the Kama river meets the Volga, in what is now central Russia, from about the 800s to 1236. Its capital was Bolghar.
